text: The standard fix for exactly this shape of bug: aggregate the many-side of the join down to one row per key, before joining. Turn the one-to-many relationship back into the one-to-one one the join was always written to assume.

A new model groups payments by order_id, summing amount — correctly combining a split payment's two amounts into the order's real total. Which is also, on reflection, what Finance actually wanted all along.

Only one part of fct_orders changes: the payments CTE now reads from this new aggregate instead of the raw staging model. The is_incremental block, the unique_key, everything else stays exactly as it was.

Full refresh is required here, not optional. The existing incremental data already has the duplicated rows baked in, and is_incremental's usual filtering would leave that old, bad data sitting there untouched. A full refresh re-derives everything under the corrected join.
